_readme: Keys exempted from the numeric-sequence check, each with a reason.
The validator normally fails a run when a figure in the English is missing
from a translation, because a dropped number in a factual sentence makes a
stated fact false. Spanish and Portuguese conventionally SPELL OUT small
numbers in prose -- '2 players' becomes 'dos jugadores' -- so the figure
stops being a figure while the claim stays identical.
Keys are named here ONE AT A TIME with a written reason, so each exemption
is a deliberate decision rather than a blanket loosening. Exempt keys still
print their mismatch on every run; they just don't fail it.
CAUTION: exempting a key removes the guard for that key in ALL languages.
If the English behind one of these changes (say 2 players becomes 4), no
check will catch a translation that keeps the old number. Re-read these by
hand when the consensus rules change.
Verified against the English source, not against the machine translation:
the Spanish and Portuguese below state the same thresholds as the English.
consensus_desc_level1: English '2 players'; es/pt-br spell it 'dos'/'duas'. Threshold unchanged.
consensus_desc_level2: English '3 players'; es/pt-br spell it 'tres'/'três'. Threshold unchanged.
